newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Asian Gold - Silver slump in U.S. drags gold down.
newsitem.headline: Asian Gold - Silver slump in U.S. drags gold down.

text.p: Asian gold prices slipped on Friday, as the yellow metal fell on follow-through selling after silver slumped overnight in New York, precious metal dealers in Hong Kong and Singapore said.

By midday, silver was trading in Hong Kong at US$4.73/75 an ounce against New York's close of $4.74. Gold took its cue and was seen ranging between $348.00/348.50 an ounce after closing on Thursday at $349.00/349.50.
"Gold followed silver down. It was that simple," a gold trader for a bank in Singapore said. "Gold may even go down to $345-$346 (an ounce) next week the way things are going."
"Gold's been under constant pressure this morning so people are standing aside," a dealer at a local securites house in Hong Kong said.

Singapore traders said silver's downside may be limited and a floor for the metal will probably be established above $4.60. "It may be difficult for silver to negotiate another 10 cents down. We'll see support coming in at that level," one dealer in the city-state said.
In Hong Kong, the securities house dealer said "sentiment is mixed on the immediate trend as most traders are focussing on silver, the U.S. dollar and stock market movements."
While soft silver prices were pressuring the yellow metal, stock market losses may also prompt investors to return to gold and bid up the price of the metal, dealers in Hong Kong said.
Asian physical demand was seen steady in Hong Kong but Singapore dealers reported the start of a seasonal slump in gold which may last several weeks.
"Physical demand was steady but dwarfed by selling pressure," a Hong Kong-based dealer said. "Support was seen at around $345 to $348 an ounce, while resistance was pegged at $355."
Singapore dealers see the yellow metal shuttling between $348 and $352 an ounce, with the chance of a major breakout on either side of the ledger seen as fairly slim.

"There is not much demand going around. It's very weak," a dealer for a North American bank in Singapore said, adding the onset of April has induced a seasonal lull in demand. "Buyers in India are quiet."

"Demand in Indonesia, India and Thailand has tailed off. Chinese buying has slowed down as well. People are expecting slower demand," a dealer for a Western financial institution added. "Buying in the region has diminished significantly."

One jeweller in Singapore estimated demand will fall by up to 20 percent in April and the slow pace of buying will last several months. It will only be interrupted by sporadic buying if prices fall to "desirable levels," the jeweller said.
"We need to see lower prices before demand can bounce back," one dealer in a bank in Singapore said.
"The only time you'll see demand re-ignite will be when gold falls below $345 (an ounce)," another trader in Singapore said.
Singapore premiums over spot London prices slipped because of soft demand. Premiums were seen at 80-120 U.S. cents from last week's 120-130 cents.
"Premiums are flat because of poor demand. There is still some level of demand in the market, but you will have to lower your premiums to attract that business," one bank dealer in Singapore said.
